title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
hints: what traversal order visits a BST's nodes from smallest to largest value?
you don't need every value up front - can you stop the traversal early once you've seen enough of them?
keep a counter that increments every time you visit a node during the inorder traversal; when the counter reaches k, that node's value is your answer
an iterative inorder traversal with an explicit stack makes it easy to stop as soon as the kth node is popped, without wasting time recursing further
commonMistakes: collecting all n values into a list and returning the kth one, which works but wastes O(n) space when an early-stopping traversal would do less work
using a preorder or postorder traversal instead of inorder, which does not visit values in sorted order
off-by-one error between 1-indexed k and a 0-indexed counter or list position

content.problemStatement:
Binary trees in these problems are encoded as a flat array named `tree`
using complete-binary-tree (heap) indexing:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`
- `-101` means "no node here" - real node values always fall between -100 and 100, so -101 can never be a genuine value

You're given a valid binary search tree encoded this way, along with an
integer `k`.

**Return the `k`th smallest value stored in the tree, using 1-indexing
(k = 1 means the smallest value in the tree).**
constraints: 1 <= k <= number of nodes in the tree
the sentinel value -101 marks a missing node and never appears as a real value
notes: k equals the total number of nodes (largest value)
a tree with a single node, so k must be 1

optimal.time: O(h + k), since you may walk down to the leftmost node first and then only need k steps of the traversal
optimal.space: O(h) for the recursion/explicit stack, without needing to store all n values
optimal.pattern: inorder traversal of a BST visits nodes in sorted order, so stop as soon as the kth value visited is found

bruteForce.approach: do a full inorder traversal to collect every value in sorted order into a list, then index into it at position k-1
